facts.text: Lawton was named for Major General Henry Ware Lawton, a Civil War hero who earned the Medal of Honor before dying in the Philippine–American War.
Old Fort Sill, just south of town, holds the distinction of being a National Historic Landmark, the highest U.S. classification for historic sites.
The War Department chose the site for Camp Doniphan after discovering 5 million gallons of water in Lake Lawtonka, sparking Lawton’s rapid growth.
The Carnegie Library, built in 1922, remains a centerpiece of Lawton’s historic downtown and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
Fort Sill’s military reservation lies directly south of Lawton, and the town’s economy has long been tied to the base’s presence.
The Museum of the Great Plains showcases natural history and early settlement stories, highlighting how European Americans shaped the region.
